title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous and next pages. 𝔖^+ is a (profinite) group, the index-2 'orientation-preserving' part of a group 𝔖 that contains elements ρ, σ, τ, τ'. L_0 ⊂ 𝔖^+ is a subgroup. Z_{ρ,σ} is a group of quadruples (u, μ, ε, ε') with u ∈ Aut(𝔖^+), μ ∈ Ẑ* and ε, ε' ∈ {±1}. There is an exact sequence 1 → L_0 → Z_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, where i_{L_0,Z}(l) = (int(l)|𝔖^+, 1, 1, 1). Γ_{ρ,σ} carries a cyclotomic-type character χ_Γ and two sign characters ε_Γ, ε'_Γ.

On p.551, Z_{ρ,σ} acts on 𝔖^+ through u, and Grothendieck forms the semidirect product S_0G = Z_{ρ,σ} ⋉ 𝔖^+.

This page does four things.
(23) It defines the 'antidiagonal' homomorphism L_0 → S_0G, l ↦ i_{L_0,Z}(l)·l^{-1}. Its image is normal, which needs Z to preserve L_0.
(24)–(25) It sets G_{ρ,σ} = S_0G / Im L_0, which gives the exact sequence 1 → L_0 → S_0G → G_{ρ,σ} → 1.
(26) It records the resulting commutative square: in G, the image of int(l) ∈ Z equals the image of l ∈ 𝔖^+. It also notes that Ker(𝔖^+ → G) ≅ Ker(L_0 → Z) = L_0 ∩ centre(𝔖^+), which hypothesis (15) makes trivial.
(27) The upshot is a morphism of extensions from 1 → L_0 → Z → Γ → 1 to 1 → 𝔖^+ → G → Γ → 1. This is the pushout of the extension Z of Γ along L_0 ↪ 𝔖^+.
(28) The characters χ, ε, ε' are pulled back to G via δ_G. On the next page Grothendieck embeds all of 𝔖 into G, sending τ' to the image of (int τ|𝔖^+, −1, −1, −1).

Purpose: to build a group G_{ρ,σ} that contains 𝔖^+, maps onto the 'Galois–Teichmüller-like' group Γ_{ρ,σ}, and carries cyclotomic and sign characters. It serves the analysis of the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets), with the centralizers Z_ρ, Z_σ treated next.

Mathematically this is the standard construction of the extension attached to an outer action when the centre is trivial: the pushout of an extension along an equivariant inclusion.
errors: (28) is miswritten. It should read χ_G = χ_Γ∘δ_G, ε_G = ε_Γ∘δ_G, ε'_G = ε'_Γ∘δ_G: the third equation lacks 'ε'_G =' and the subscripts γ should be Γ.
Normality of Im L_0 in S_0G implicitly needs u(L_0) = L_0 for (u,…) ∈ Z, compatible with int. This is presumably built into the definition of Z_{ρ,σ} on earlier pages; it is not restated here.
Not an error, an inference: the sign l^{-1} together with int(l) is consistent if 𝔖^+ acts via u. Exactness of the bottom row of (27) follows from Z/L_0 = Γ and from the injectivity given by (15).

ideas.what: G = (Z ⋉ 𝔖^+)/{(int l, l^{-1}) : l ∈ L_0}: pushout of the extension 1→L_0→Z→Γ→1 along L_0 ↪ 𝔖^+
ideas.modern_name: pushout of group extensions / extension induced by an outer action (trivial centre case)
ideas.where_published: Analogous constructions are standard in SGA 1 Exp. XIII-type settings and in the GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara); exact source unsure

ideas.what: Kernel of 𝔖^+ → G equals L_0 ∩ centre(𝔖^+); trivial under a centre-freeness hypothesis
ideas.modern_name: faithfulness of the induced extension when the centre is trivial

ideas.what: Pulling the cyclotomic character and two sign characters back to G
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cyclotomic character on GT-type groups)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic bookkeeping: forming an extension as a pushout via a semidirect product modulo an antidiagonal subgroup. It is technical infrastructure for the larger 'équation des lacets' programme and contains no new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: The group written 𝔖^+ here and 𝔊^+ on p.551 is the same Gothic letter; the transcriptions should be made consistent.
(28) in the image reads roughly 'χ_G = χ_Γ∘δ_G, ε_G = ε_Γ∘δ_G, ε'_Γ∘δ_G'. 'γ_G = γ_γ' is a misreading of χ_G = χ_Γ.
The struck words after 'sous-groupe invariant' are a cancelled 'On a par définition'.
